text:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV 1 - multi-GPU communicator ghosting detected on cluster-gpu-prod-7. Affected jobs: tj-2026-train-3, gen-infer-prod-9. Symptoms: allreduce hangs, worker processes idle with CUDA kernel stalls. Started 2026-03-15T04:15:01Z. Paging oncall: @asha.

asha: I'm on it. joining bridge, pulling logs now.

ben: saw alerts for increased op latency + GPU utilization flatline. could be NCCL deadlock or driver X timeout (Xid 79).

mike: +1 to NCCL hang. last change was kernel bump yesterday on nodes in pool gpuprod-slice-b. rolling restarts started at 03:40 UTC.

cassandra: does this impact customer-facing endpoints? which jobs are user-facing?

ben: gen-infer-prod-9 is a low-latency endpoint backed by a dedicated alloc; requests are 503-ing. tj-2026 is internal batch training, lower priority.

asha: quick impact summary: ~6 endpoints behind the allocator failing requests (5% error spike), 2 long-running training jobs stalled. tagging customer-impact for the incident.

eric: are nodes flapping or just processes stuck? any OOMs in dmesg?

mike: grabbing dmesg and nvidia-smi from the affected node node-g7-14 (IP 10.3.7.214). hold.

mike: ```bash
# nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu --format=csv
index, name, utilization.gpu [%], utilization.memory [%], temperature.gpu [C]
0, A100-SXM4-80GB, 0 %, 1 %, 46 C
1, A100-SXM4-80GB, 0 %, 1 %, 45 C
2, A100-SXM4-80GB, 0 %, 1 %, 46 C
3, A100-SXM4-80GB, 0 %, 1 %, 46 C
```

mike: processes still present but NVSM shows no SM activity. dmesg has repeated: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79` and `nvidia_uvm: CPU fault on GPU` entries.

ben: Xid 79 often points to a kernel-level GPU reset or driver hang. did the earlier kernel bump include any MIG or driver changes?

mike: kernel 6.1.12 -> 6.1.13 applied. driver stayed at 535.54.02. can't see driver module reloads in logs.

asha: immediate mitigation: can we drain the node and force restart the runtime containers for the affected jobs? need to avoid noisy restarts if it impacts running inferences badly.

eric: recommend cordon+drain node-g7-14, then try `systemctl restart redwood-runtime` on the node. also capture full /var/log/syslog and container logs first.

mike: starting log bundle now: ```bash
sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime -o cat --no-pager > /tmp/runtime.log
sudo cp /var/log/syslog /tmp/syslog
kubectl -n ml logs --tail=500 job/tj-2026-train-3 > /tmp/tj.log || true
```

deploy-bot: Automation: created incident-runbook checkpoint cp_3345678901 (https://runbooks.redwood/3345678901).

ben: FYI I see NCCL INFO: `ncclCommInitRank()` succeeded then later `ncclAllReduce` stalled. stack traces show the worker stuck in `libnccl.so` inside `collNetLL`.

mike: I'm going to try a graceful runtime restart on node-g7-14 now. if that doesn't free the kernel we escalate to host reboot. Will run after logs are uploaded.

asha: please coordinate with ops. I'll update customers on impacted endpoints at 04:35 UTC.

mike: runtime restart output: ```
sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime
# took ~8s, runtime logs show container exit with code 137 for worker containers
# attempting to reattach communicator
```

eric: code 137 suggests OOM kill. are we hitting device memory exhaustion? check cgroup and dmesg for oom-killer.

mike: no user-space OOM messages. kernel still showing repeated Xid 79 and UVM page faults. after runtime restart, containers start but collective still stalls.

ben: suspects: 1) driver bug triggered by kernel bump; 2) persistent NCCL state needs GPU reset; 3) rare PCI bus instability.

asha: escalate plan: (A) cordon node and evacuate; (B) if evacuation fails, force reboot the host; (C) if multiple nodes show same signature, fallback routing to smaller model shards (single-GPU) for customer endpoints.

cassandra: can we fallback the gen-infer-prod-9 pool to 1-GPU model variant without significant config churn? we need to reduce customer errors in the meantime.

mike: yes, config supports model-variant fallback. I'll prepare a canary that re-routes 20% traffic to single-GPU variant.

ben: note: single-GPU variant increases latency ~2x. ops and SRE, confirm customer SLAs and whether acceptable.

asha: go ahead with 20% canary, monitor 5m. if stable, ramp to 100%. update status: "mitigating - routing fallback in progress".

deploy-bot: Automation: started rollout job rr-3345678901 to route 20% to model-variant sgv-3.

mike: cordon+drain node-g7-14 now: ```bash
kubectl cordon node-g7-14
kubectl drain node-g7-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60
```

mike: drain hung on one stateful job (tj-2026) that refuses to terminate; it's stuck in Terminating state because process won't die inside container.

eric: escalate to host-level kill: `crictl stopp` + `crictl rm` then `systemctl restart containerd`. if still stuck, schedule host reboot with maintenance tag.

mike: performed `crictl stopp` then `crictl rm`. container removed. drain completed. moving node to maintenance and rebooting.

mike: reboot in progress. kernel shows GPU resets during boot with `nvidia: GPU reset done`. hoping a full host reboot clears GPU state.

ben: while rebooting, monitoring other nodes for similar Xid79 flood. grep across recent syslogs: `grep -R "Xid (PCI" /var/log/* | wc -l` shows no other nodes with repeated hits. looks isolated to slice-b nodes with kernel 6.1.13.

asha: update to customers: posted to status page: "Investigating GPU infrastructure issue affecting some inference requests. Mitigation in progress: traffic canaryed to single-GPU variant; affected host is being rebooted. Next update in 20 minutes." :warning:

cassandra: thanks. coordinate with success for proactive outreach if ramp persists.

mike: node back up. post-reboot dmesg shows Xid 79 frequency reduced to a handful during boot, none during normal runtime. restarting affected jobs.

ben: after restart, NCCL collectives resumed on restarted workers; allreduce completed for tj-2026. gen-infer-prod-9 canary at 20% stable for 8m with no errors.

asha: ramping canary to 100% now.

deploy-bot: Rollout rr-3345678901 updated: 100% traffic routed to sg-variant sgv-3.

mike: monitoring: latencies increased as expected but error rate returning to baseline. no further Xid 79 reports on the node.

eric: next steps: (1) keep node cordoned until kernel rollback or driver update validated; (2) create postmortem with timeline + remediation; (3) consider blacklisting kernel 6.1.13 for GPU nodes until we root cause.

ben: also recommend adding automated detection for repeating Xid 79 across nodes and auto-evacuate if count > 10 in 5m.

asha: agreed. assigning postmortem to @mike and @ben. I'll file a customer impact report for the overnight incidents.

cassandra: hold on follow-up: product will draft customer note for affected accounts. tagging support for outreach.

mike: creating postmortem draft link: https://pm.redwood/incidents/3345678901-pm (will attach logs and kernel traces).

incident-bot: Incident status changed to Resolved by asha at 2026-03-15T05:30:25Z.

asha: thanks team. great coordination. actions: kernel blocklist, Xid alerting, postmortem + customer comms. closing channel in 1h unless new regressions."
